Venom isn’t slowing down,it's expanding its toolkit and setting up for a much bigger phase of digital infrastructure.

For years, Venom has delivered what governments, banks, and enterprises need most: low fees, massive scalability, and real-time performance.
Now, they’re building on that foundation again.

Adoption is already taking shape:
– The Philippines is using Venom in its national digitalization plans
– The UAE runs its carbon credit system on Venom
– A major fintech company in China is in active discussions

And now comes the major upgrade.

x402 is coming to @VenomFoundation
This integration will allow automated systems to settle payments instantly no delays, no congestion, just direct execution on the network.

For developers
A simplified SDK is on the way, supporting JavaScript, Python, Rust, Go, and more.
A few lines of code will be all it takes to connect.

This upgrade strengthens Venom’s core strengths and opens space for new tools and advanced system interactions.

With dynamic sharding and a target of 500,000 daily transactions, Venom is ready for the next level of demand.

A new chapter is unfolding and this move sets the pace for what comes next.

You can also check out the campaign on @BingXOfficial with $13,000 up for grabs
Join here: https://t.co/WytxjYmxXG

Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 5 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Shear Line
Issued at: 5:00 AM, 25 November 2025(Tuesday)

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Quezon, Metro Manila, Rizal, Laguna, Cavite, Batangas, Bulacan and Nueva Ecija(Gabaldon, Gapan, Palayan, Laur, Penaranda, Bongabon, General Tinio).
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, light to moderate rains affecting Tarlac, Pampanga, Zambales, Bataan and Nueva Ecija(Cabiao, San Antonio, San Isidro, Aliaga, Cabanatuan, Carranglan, Cuyapo, General Mamerto Natividad, Guimba, Jaen, Licab, Llanera, Lupao, Nampicuan, Pantabangan, Quezon, Rizal, San Jose, San Leonardo, Santa Rosa, Santo Domingo, Munoz, Talavera, Talugtug, Zaragoza) which may persist within 3 hours.
The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 8:00 AM today.

For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZJq1n.
